analysis: Examined base_text units of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1-797) and the only changed range (head 1030-1047, outside the supplied base excerpts but visible in the complete patch excerpt). The change is documentation only. It describes a new PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge (provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Prompting/PromptTokenCache.swift). That cache splits rendered prompts at added-token boundaries and reuses token IDs per prefix-cache scope. It also uses parallel encoding on up to four cores and ChatTemplateLoopRewrites for linear-time Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS rendering. Mismatches against the unchanged applyChatTemplate path are detected by load-time and sampled background comparisons. The kill switch is DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0. Security relevance: T-041/SEC-035 (cross-tenant cache reuse and TTFT oracle) and A-001 (prompt plaintext held in memory). The doc states that reuse never crosses a cache scope. That scope is the coordinator-authored, authenticated cacheSalt (T-041 mitigation). If the claim holds, this adds a same-scope tokenization timing signal of the same kind as the accepted SEC-035, not a cross-account one. Unverified items for integration, because the implementation source was not supplied: (1) The cache key must include the authenticated scope and not a caller prompt_cache_key or user field. (2) Behavior when a request has no scope, e.g. standalone/local mode or Super slots that are off without a scope, matters, since 'when caching is enabled for the request' is ambiguous. (3) Retention bounds, memory charging and eviction for cached token pieces, given that this text is decrypted prompt content held in process (A-001, TB-007/T-028). (4) Whether a mismatch or a template rejection of a cached render fails safe to the unchanged path for the triggering request, so the served prompt is still correct (T-007 integrity). (5) DoS bounds on the four-core encoding. No concrete regression is evidenced from docs alone, so no finding is raised. The threat model's T-041 may need an entry for this new in-memory, scope-partitioned token cache.
